blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Open sort menu traps the keyboard: Tab is captured and Escape does nothing) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: WCAG 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap / 2.1.1 Keyboard, blocks keyboard and screen reader users. A keyboard user opens "Sort", focus moves into the menu; pressing Tab (or Shift+Tab, which also has event.key "Tab" and moves forward) only cycles among the four items, and Escape is not handled, so the only way out is to activate an item — the user cannot dismiss the menu and reach the product list without picking a sort order. Follow the APG menu button pattern: stop calling preventDefault on Tab and let Tab / Shift+Tab close the menu and move focus naturally; handle Escape to close the menu and return focus to the button (button.current?.focus()); also close it when focus leaves the list (onBlur with relatedTarget outside). Alternatively use a native <select> labelled "Sort", which provides all of this.
findings.title: Open sort menu traps the keyboard: Tab is captured and Escape does nothing

findings.evidence: <button ref={button} type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" onClick={() => setOpen(!open)}>
findings.recommendation: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value, misleads screen reader users. aria-expanded is a hard-coded string, so after activating "Sort" the button is still announced as "collapsed" while the menu is open, and the state never matches the behaviour. Bind it to the state: aria-expanded={open}; optionally add aria-controls pointing to the menu's id.
findings.title: Menu button always announces `aria-expanded="false"`
